lesson.title: Everyday Idioms in Action
lesson.subtitle: tener ganas de ('to feel like'), darse cuenta de ('to realize'), de repente ('suddenly')

hook.title: Expressing 'I Feel Like...' and 'In Fact'
hook.content: Whether you are choosing a restaurant or planning a trip, tener hambre, tener sed, tener razón, and de hecho ('in fact') make your Spanish sound immediately warm and idiomatic.

pattern.title: La Cuenta: Both 'The Restaurant Bill' and 'Account'
pattern.content: Notice how la cuenta (from contar 'to count', o→ue) means 'the bill/check' in a restaurant (La cuenta, por favor) AND 'account/realization' inside darse cuenta de!

exercises.prompt: Match each English expression with its Spanish partner:
exercises.target_answer: la cuenta, la cuenta, por favor, de hecho, tienes toda la razón, tengo mucha sed
exercises.meaning: the bill / the account, the bill, please, in fact / actually, you are completely right, I am very thirsty
exercises.explanation: Concrete nouns power everyday Spanish idioms.

exercises.prompt: What are you asking the waiter for when you say '¿Me trae la cuenta, por favor?'?
exercises.meaning: Will you bring me the bill, please?
exercises.explanation: la cuenta is literally 'the count' of what you ordered.

exercises.prompt: Assemble: 'Will you bring me the bill, please?'
exercises.target_answer: Me traes la cuenta por favor
exercises.meaning: Will you bring me the bill, please?
exercises.explanation: ¿Me traes la cuenta, por favor? (from traer 'to bring').

exercises.idea: say: 'You are right, I want to eat'
cues: You are right (you have reason) → Tienes razón
I want to eat → quiero comer
idea_parts: I want to eat → quiero comer
exercises.meaning: You are right, I want to eat

exercises.prompt: Listen and write the whole sentence.
exercises.spoken: La cuenta por favor y muchas gracias
exercises.target_answer: La cuenta por favor y muchas gracias
exercises.meaning: The bill, please, and thank you very much
cues: and thank you very much: y muchas gracias
exercises.explanation: La cuenta, por favor, y muchas gracias.

summary.outcome: Use la cuenta, de hecho, tener razón, and traer in everyday social settings.

use_example.german: Tienes razón — ¿me traes la cuenta, por favor?
use_example.english: You are right — will you bring me the bill, please?

tener.etymology_derivation: Latin tenēre ('to hold'). While other tongues used 'have' (like French avoir), Spanish promoted 'hold' (tener) to main possession.

tengo.etymology_derivation: Latin teneō developed an epenthetic velar g: tengo.

tienes.etymology_derivation: Stem vowel e diphthongizes to ie when stressed: tienes.

cuenta.etymology_derivation: The restaurant bill is literally 'the count' (la cuenta).

hecho.english_meaning: done, made (participle of hacer); fact (el hecho)
hecho.shift_rule: Double sound shift: factum → hecho (f→h AND ct→ch!)
hecho.etymology_derivation: Look at Latin factum → Spanish hecho: initial f- became silent h-, AND medial -ct- became -ch-!

razón.context_translation: You are completely right (lit. You have all the reason).
razón.etymology_derivation: To be right in Spanish is to 'have reason': tienes razón.

hambre.context_translation: I am very hungry (lit. I have much hunger).
hambre.etymology_derivation: Feminine noun (mucha hambre) that takes el in the singular like el agua, and shows f- → h- from Latin famēs!

comer.etymology_derivation: Latin com- ('completely') + edere ('to eat', cousin of English edible and eat).

visitar.etymology_derivation: visitation → visitar. No preposition 'to' needed in Spanish: quiero visitar (two words where English needs three).
